Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answer up front: Redwood's June 2025 external penetration test (engagement with third‑party firm NorthBridge Security) covered the Redwood‑managed control plane and all Redwood‑hosted inference services (our shared Hosted endpoints) and the Redwood side of Dedicated pools. Private deployments have two variants; the parts managed by Redwood (control plane, management APIs) were included when Redwood operates them, but customer‑managed infrastructure (customer VM hosts, on‑prem networks, and their KMS) are out of scope unless we run a customer‑scoped engagement.

High level:
- Hosted (shared): INCLUDED (control plane, API layer, hosted inference nodes)
- Dedicated (Redwood‑managed GPU pool): INCLUDED for Redwood components and customer isolation boundaries; we do not test customer application logic that runs on your side
- Private (Redwood Private with Redwood‑managed control plane in customer VPC): CONTROL PLANE INCLUDED; any customer‑managed bridges/agents or self‑hosted storage not managed by Redwood are OUT OF SCOPE
- On‑prem (customer fully manages hosts/offline air‑gapped): OUT OF SCOPE unless explicitly contracted

Attachments: I attached the executive summary and a remediation tracker for Acme with current statuses. Brief notes: no outstanding Criticals; two High findings were remediated in July; three Mediums are in progress with target close by 2025‑09‑05.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share the executive summary and remediation tracker (attached).
2) If you need Redwood to include customer‑managed components we can provide a scoped SOW and a third‑party pen test estimated at 3–4 weeks once access is scheduled.
3) If Acme requires the tests to run against your Private/VPC setup on your network, we’ll need an ATO checklist and connectivity window; pricing depends on access method.

Hi Alex —

I’ll keep this concise and technical:

1) Logging and buckets
- Hosted (shared) and Dedicated (Redwood‑managed): request traces and observability logs are written to Redwood‑managed object storage. Buckets are logically segmented per‑customer (single‑tenant namespaces) and encrypted at rest with RBAC restricting access to the infra/security team. Sensitive fields are redacted before long‑term storage (we remove full request bodies and only retain metadata and sampled traces by default).
- For Redwood Private deployments that integrate with customer‑owned storage, we recommend configuring customer‑owned buckets; when configured that way, logs are written to a customer bucket and Redwood does not have write access unless explicitly granted.

2) KV cache and ephemeral state
- KV cache and model state are kept in memory and on ephemeral local storage on GPU hosts. We do not persist KV cache to object storage under normal operation. Any checkpointing to durable storage is part of an opt‑in backup workflow and must be explicitly configured. Secrets (keys/KMS materials) are never persisted in plaintext and are handled via integration with customer or Redwood KMS depending on deployment.

3) Pen test scope details
- The June 2025 engagement included both external perimeter testing and authenticated API fuzzing for Redwood‑managed services. The engagement also included internal privileged flows for Redwood infrastructure components (i.e., escalation paths inside our management plane).
- The engagement did NOT include customer application logic, customer‑managed on‑prem hosts, or customer network segmentation unless a customer‑scoped test was arranged.

If you want, we can produce a short appendix that maps these behaviors to SIG/CAIQ questions (I can draft that and attach). For on‑prem or customer host testing, we offer a paid, customer‑scoped pen test with a defined SOW and a 3–6 week timeline depending on depth.

—Mina
